prompt.context: Your friend Megan Black calls you to ask for your advice. Megan had been working in the beauty industry as an independent hair stylist for 2 years when the owner of Salon Deluxe approached her and asked her to buy the salon. It has always been her dream to own a hair salon, but she isn't sure if she should do it, or focus on her current business, Megan Black Balayage (MBB). She wants your help to figure out what she should do.
prompt.question: Should Megan buy Salon Deluxe or continue running her existing business, Megan Black Balayage? Her primary goal is to evaluate which business has the greatest NPV.

clarifying_info.a: Balayage is a technique that paints the hair to achieve a more natural looking hair dye experience.

clarifying_info.q: What is Salon Deluxe's business model?
clarifying_info.a: The salon is a high-end hair salon that specializes in balayage. The business has two segments, services and products. Appointments are booked centrally, through the salon's booking portal, and clients see 1 of 4 contractor employee stylists.

clarifying_info.q: What does a balayage appointment consist of?
clarifying_info.a: A balayage appointment has 3 parts: hair & product prep (10 mins), hair painting (90 minutes), drying & styling (50 minutes).

clarifying_info.q: Does Megan have specific metrics or goals related to this project?
clarifying_info.a: Her goal is primarily to evaluate which business has the greatest NPV.

exhibits.title: Megan Black Balayage P&L
exhibits.shows: P&L data for Megan Black Balayage including number of clients, visit frequency, average spend per visit, services margin, monthly rent, and a bar chart showing product prices for Shampoo and Conditioner with a note that all product margins are 50%.
exhibits.data: # of clients: 200; Visit frequency: Quarterly; Average spend per visit: $150; Services Margin: 60%; Rent: $500/month; Shampoo price: $60; Conditioner price: $55; Product margins: all 50%

exhibits.title: Salon Deluxe Floor Plan
exhibits.shows: A floor plan of Salon Deluxe with labeled rooms.
exhibits.data: Rooms: Hair Stations, Waiting Area/Reception, Break Room, Storage (x2)

exhibits.title: Salon Deluxe Selected Information
exhibits.shows: Key operating metrics for Salon Deluxe.
exhibits.data: Salon Hours: 10 AM - 7 PM, 5 days/week; Stylists take a daily 1-hour break; Average appt. duration: 2.5 hours; Average spend per appt: $150; Stylist Revenue Share: 65% of service revenue; Total requested appts: 6,000; Rent: $4k/month; Net Profit from Product Sales: $10k/year; Salon Discount Rate: 10%

framework: NPV of Megan Black Balayage: calculate annual service profit (clients x visit frequency x price x margin), add product profit, subtract rent, divide by hurdle rate

NPV of Salon Deluxe: calculate salon capacity from operating hours and appointment duration, determine occupancy vs. demand, calculate service profit (capacity x price x salon margin after stylist share), add product profit, subtract rent, divide by discount rate
Compare NPVs to determine which business delivers more value to Megan
Internal considerations: buy vs. build option; initiatives to improve NPV (capacity expansion, cost reduction, marketing); Megan's risk profile, managerial experience, culture fit with new team
External considerations: local competition, customer preferences, availability of local talent

questions.prompt: What is MBB's (Megan Black Balayage's) annual profit and NPV?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute service revenue from 200 clients visiting quarterly at $150 each, apply the 60% margin, then calculate product profit. They will not have penetration rates for products and should ask - provide shampoo 25% and conditioner 20% when asked. After finding annual profit, divide by the hurdle rate (provide 5% if asked). Strong candidates recognize that MBB's NPV is a benchmark against which to compare the acquisition.

math.setup: Services: clients x visits/year x price/visit x margin. Products: annual visits x penetration rate x price x 50% margin. Annual profit = service profit + product profit - annual rent. NPV = annual profit / hurdle rate.
steps: Shampoo (penetration 25%, provide if asked): 800 x 25% = 200 bottles x $60 = $12,000 x 50% = $6,000
Conditioner (penetration 20%, provide if asked): 800 x 20% = 160 bottles x $55 = $8,800 x 50% = $4,400

questions.prompt: What is the NPV of owning Salon Deluxe?
questions.guidance: Candidate must derive salon capacity from operating data: 8 working hours per day (9 hours minus 1-hour break) divided by 2.5-hour appointments equals 3.2 appointments per stylist per day; times 250 working days times 4 stylists equals 3,200 annual capacity. Requested appointments of 6,000 exceed capacity, so the salon runs at 100% occupancy. Salon margin is 35% (100% minus 65% stylist revenue share). Excellent candidates will note that the current NPV ($1.3M) is below MBB ($1.52M) but spot that two unused storage rooms on the floor plan represent an untapped capacity opportunity. Note: if the candidate asks what happens to Megan's existing clients, tell them she will need to give them up to focus on operating Salon Deluxe.

math.setup: Capacity: (working hours/day / appt duration) x working days/year x number of stylists. Service profit: capacity x price x (1 - stylist share) - annual rent. NPV: (service profit + product profit) / discount rate.
steps: Working hours per day: 9 hours (10 AM-7 PM) minus 1-hour break = 8 hours
Working days per year: 5 days/week x 50 weeks = 250 days
Capacity per stylist per year: 3.2 x 250 = 800 appts
math.answer: Annual profit: $130,000; NPV: approximately $1.3M (below MBB NPV of $1.52M; unused storage space is a key upside opportunity)

questions.prompt: What are some levers Megan could pull to make Salon Deluxe a more attractive business? Which might have the largest impact?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm across revenue and cost levers. Key insight: the salon runs at 100% capacity, so marketing, loyalty programs, and discounts will not help - the constraint is supply, not demand. The floor plan reveals two unused storage rooms, which is the most impactful lever. Guide candidate toward unused space if not mentioned. Interviewer responses to specific levers: rent is locked in a long-term contract; price increases are difficult in a competitive market; marketing/loyalty programs add no value at full capacity.

questions.prompt: If Megan converts the unused storage space into a drying and styling station at a cost of $100k (renovation and assistant hire), each stylist can increase capacity by 37.5%. What is the new projected NPV of the business?
questions.guidance: Candidate applies 37.5% capacity increase to original service profit, subtracts interest on the $100k renovation investment, adds product profit, subtracts rent, divides by discount rate, then deducts the upfront renovation cost. Exceptional candidates will compute the maximum price Megan should pay for the salon by taking the difference between the new Salon Deluxe NPV and MBB NPV.

math.setup: New service profit = original service profit x 1.375. Annual interest on renovation = $100k x discount rate. NPV = (new service profit + product profit - interest - rent) / discount rate - renovation cost.
steps: New service profit after 37.5% capacity increase: $168,000 x 1.375 = $231,000
math.answer: New NPV: approximately $1.73M; Maximum price Megan should pay for Salon Deluxe: approximately $210k

brainstorming.prompt: What are some levers we could pull to make Salon Deluxe a more attractive business? Which of these ideas might have the largest impact?

categories.name: Increase Service Revenue
ideas: Increase salon capacity by converting unused storage rooms into a drying and styling station
Introduce a loyalty program to encourage more frequent visits
Raise prices if the market is not too competitive
Build or buy a second salon location

categories.name: Decrease Service Costs
ideas: Cut low-margin services from the menu
Source products from new vendors to reduce COGS
Evaluate and restructure the stylist profit-share arrangement

categories.name: Increase Product Profitability
ideas: Offer promotional discounts to drive higher product sales volume
Add complementary products or bundles such as hairspray and styling creams
Switch to smaller bottle sizes to lower per-unit cost
Find new vendors with lower wholesale costs
Invest in website SEO to drive online product sales

categories.name: Financing
ideas: Pay down debt to reduce interest expense
Refinance the renovation loan at a lower interest rate

recommendation: Under base conditions Megan should keep running MBB, whose NPV (~$1.52M) exceeds Salon Deluxe's base NPV (~$1.3M)
If Megan acquires Salon Deluxe below ~$210k and executes the storage-room renovation, the post-renovation NPV (~$1.73M) exceeds MBB and makes the acquisition worthwhile
risks: Megan must give up her MBB clients if she takes over Salon Deluxe, forfeiting ~$1.52M in value unless the acquisition price accounts for this
Renovation cost and capacity projections are estimates and carry execution risk
Any service disruption during renovation directly reduces revenue at a 100%-capacity salon
As an independent stylist, Megan may lack managerial experience to run a multi-stylist operation
A competitive local market limits the ability to raise prices to offset cost increases
next_steps: Negotiate the Salon Deluxe purchase price below the $210k threshold identified by the NPV analysis
Commission a detailed feasibility study for the storage room conversion
Assess Megan's readiness for managing a team of four stylists
Evaluate the local competitive landscape to validate pricing and demand assumptions
